title: Catalytic Phosphorus(V)-Mediated Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions: Development of a Catalytic Appel Reaction
authors: Denton, Ross M.; An, Jie; Adeniran, Beatrice; Blake, Alexander J.; Lewis, William; Poulton, Andrew M.
reference: Catalytic Phosphorus(V)-Mediated Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions: Development of a Catalytic Appel Reaction | Denton, Ross M.; An, Jie; Adeniran, Beatrice; Blake, Alexander J.; Lewis, William; Poulton, Andrew M. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2011), 76(16), 6749-6767
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure 3. To a solution of triphenylphosphine oxide (42 mg, 0.15 mmol) in either CHCl3 or CDCl3 (1.5 mL) were added oxalyl chloride (16.5 μL, 0.195mmol) and LiBr (130-304mg, 1.50-3.50 mmol), and the reaction mixture stirred for 5 min. The appropriate alcohol (1.00 equiv) and oxalyl chloride (93.5 μL, 1.11 mmol) as solutions in either CHCl3 or CDCl3 (1.0 mL) were then added simultaneously over 5 h via syringe pump at rt. The reaction mixture was filtered. The solvent was removed in vacuo. Further purification by flash chromatography (silica, 5-10% Et2O/petroleum ether) gave the pure bromides. 1-Bromodec-2-yne (11f) as a colorless oil, yield 163 mg, 75%. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δ 3.93 (t, J = 2.3 Hz, 2H, CCCH2Cl), 2.24 (m, 2H, H2CCH2CC), 1.51 (m, 2H, H2CCH2CH2CC), 1.41-1.24 (m, 8H, 4 x CH2CH3), 0.89 (t, J = 7.0 Hz, 3H, CH3); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) δ 88.4, 75.3, 31.7, 28.8, 28.8, 28.4, 22.7, 19.0, 15.9, 14.1.
notes: Appel reaction, slow simultaneous addition of alcohol and oxalyl chloride stage 2

authors: Newman, Stephen G.; Bryan, Christopher S.; Perez, Didier; Lautens, Mark
reference: The use of bromotrichloromethane in chlorination reactions | Newman, Stephen G.; Bryan, Christopher S.; Perez, Didier; Lautens, Mark | Synthesis (2011), (2), 342-346
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: Benzyl Chlorides 4 from Alcohols 3; General Procedure B: Ph3P (3 equiv) and CH2Cl2 (2 mL per 3.0 mmol Ph3P) were added to a flask equipped with a magnetic stir bar. CBrCl3 (1.2 equiv) was added, the flask was closed with a septum, and the mixture was stirred under air at r.t. for 40 min, during which the colorless soln turned deep brown. A soln of the requisite alcohol 3 (1.0 equiv) in CH2Cl2 (3 mL per 1.0 mmol alcohol) was added dropwise, and the mixture was stirred at r.t. until the starting material had been consumed (as indicated by TLC; approximately 10 min). The mixture was diluted with a Et2O-pentane mixture (3:1) until solid Ph3PO began to precipitate. The heterogeneous mixture was then filtered through a pad of silica gel, which was rinsed with a Et2O-pentane mixture (3:1). Rotary evaporation provided clean 4 after most reactions, as indicated by 1H NMR spectroscopy. The products were purified additionally by flash chromatography. The product was purified by flash column chromatography (silica gel, pentane); this provided 4a. 2-Chloro-1,2-bis(4-methoxyphenyl)ethanone (4f): General procedure B was followed (1 mmol scale). The product was purified by recrystallization from Et2O-pentane; this provided 4f as a white solid. reference: Catalytic Phosphorus(V)-Mediated Nucleophilic Substitution Reactions: Development of a Catalytic Appel Reaction | Denton, Ross M.; An, Jie; Adeniran, Beatrice; Blake, Alexander J.; Lewis, William; Poulton, Andrew M. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2011), 76(16), 6749-6767
experimental_procedure: General/Typical Procedure: General Procedure 3. To a solution of triphenylphosphine oxide (42 mg, 0.15 mmol) in either CHCl3 or CDCl3 (1.5 mL) were added oxalyl chloride (16.5 μL, 0.195mmol) and LiBr (130-304mg, 1.50-3.50 mmol), and the reaction mixture stirred for 5 min. The appropriate alcohol (1.00 equiv) and oxalyl chloride (93.5 μL, 1.11 mmol) as solutions in either CHCl3 or CDCl3 (1.0 mL) were then added simultaneously over 5 h via syringe pump at rt. The reaction mixture was filtered. The solvent was removed in vacuo. Further purification by flash chromatography (silica, 5-10% Et2O/petroleum ether) gave the pure bromides. 1-Bromoethyl Benzene (11m), yield 137 mg, 74%. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3) δ 7.48-7.28 (m, 5H, ArH), 5.25 (q, J = 6.9 Hz, 1H, ClCH), 2.08 (d, J = 6.9 Hz, 3H, CH3); 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3) δ 143.3, 128.7, 128.4, 126.9, 49.6, 26.9.
notes: Appel reaction, slow simultaneous addition of alcohol and oxalyl chloride stage 2

authors: Danilkina, N. A.; Kulyashova, A. E.; Khlebnikov, A. F.; Brase, S.; Balova, I. A.
reference: Electrophilic Cyclization of Aryldiacetylenes in the Synthesis of Functionalized Enediynes Fused to a Heterocyclic Core | Danilkina, N. A.; Kulyashova, A. E.; Khlebnikov, A. F.; Brase, S.; Balova, I. A. | Journal of Organic Chemistry (2014), 79(19), 9018-9045
experimental_procedure: Methyl 2,3-Bis(6-iodohex-1-yn-1-yl)-1-methyl-1H-indole-5-carboxylate (21). To a degassed stirred solution of indole 17g (0.49 mmol, 185 mg) in anhydrous THF (5.0 mL) were added PPh3 (1.07 mmol, 280 mg) and imidazole (1.47 mmol, 100 mg). After a homogeneous solution had formed, the reaction mixture was cooled to −20 °C, and I2 (1.18 mmol, 300 mg) was added. The mixture obtained was stirred at −20 °C for 1 h, the cooling bath was removed, and the reaction mixture was allowed to warm to room temperature, diluted with a saturated solution of NaHCO3, and stirred at 0 °C. The precipitate was filtered off and washed three times with Et2O. The ether layer was separated, and the water layer was extracted with Et2O. Combined organic layers were washed with Na2S2O3 and brine, dried over anhydrous Na2SO4, and concentrated under reduced pressure to yield the crude product, which was purified by column chromatography using cyclohexane/ethyl acetate (15:1 → 5:1) as the eluent. 276 mg (94%) of 21 as a beige solid. Mp 63−65 °C. 1H NMR (400 MHz, CDCl3, δ): 1.76−1.85 (m, 4H), 2.04−2.13 (m, 4H), 2.59− 2.66 (m, 4H), 3.26−3.31 (m, 4H), 3.77 (s, 3H), 3.94 (s, 3H), 7.24 (d, J = 8.7 Hz, 1H), 7.95 (dd, J = 8.7 Hz, J = 1.3 Hz, 1H), 8.38 (s, 1H). 13C NMR (100 MHz, CDCl3, δ): 5.9, 6.4, 18.9, 29.2, 29.7, 31.1, 32.4, 32.6, 51.9, 71.5 (Cq), 73.2 (Cq), 94.3 (Cq), 100.1 (Cq), 104.1 (Cq), 109.1, 122.5 (Cq), 122.9, 124.8, 126.9 (Cq), 127.6 (Cq), 138.3 (Cq), 167.8, one signal overlaps with others.
